investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes advertising the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM never started.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 122s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 141s, latencyMs=145922 — confirms the scheduling failure is not a transient single-pod event.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 145s, latencyMs=151951 — all three remote-agent checks share the same scheduler rejection pattern.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence fields were written, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-ready state.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 (createAgent call) never returned successfully.

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-259): contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because no evidence was produced.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130672 — the probe ran for ~130 s before failing, consistent with a scheduling timeout rather than an immediate API error.
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the two kata/peerpods nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods; if those 2 nodes are also at capacity, no fallback exists. A misconfigured or overly narrow selector would shrink the eligible pool further.

Cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is set too low relative to concurrent demand: multiple simultaneous eval runs or production workloads may be competing for the same finite VM slots.
Peerpods node pool is under-provisioned or a node in the pool is NotReady/cordoned: if one of the two kata-capable nodes is unavailable, effective capacity is halved, making exhaustion more likely.

Preemption policy on the remote-agent pod or the occupying pods prevents eviction: the scheduler explicitly reported 'No preemption victims found', meaning existing pods on those nodes are protected from preemption (e.g., PriorityClass or PodDisruptionBudget).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (allocatable > requested) on the two eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node affinity misconfiguration or API-level failure.

If the remote-agent pod spec's node affinity or selector was recently changed to exclude the kata-capable nodes entirely, the 'Insufficient' message would be a secondary symptom and the affinity misconfiguration would be the primary cause.

If a subsequent eval run immediately succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent workloads temporarily exhausted slots), not a sustained capacity problem.
If the two kata-capable nodes were NotReady or cordoned at the time of the run, the root cause would be node availability rather than resource exhaustion.

If the eval runner itself had a configuration error that caused it to request more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than intended per pod, the cluster capacity might be sufficient but the per-pod request would be wrong.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability (allocatable minus requested) on each eligible node and warns before exhaustion reaches 100%, providing earlier signal than a scheduling timeout.
Add a latency-band eval for remote-agent pod scheduling time that warns when scheduling exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s) well before the 122s+ stuck-pod failure observed here.
Add an eval that verifies the count of Running pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots stays below a configured high-water mark, catching capacity creep before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a node-readiness eval that checks all kata-capable nodes are in Ready state and untainted, so node-level availability issues are caught independently of the agent creation flow.
Consider a sibling eval that checks preemption policy configuration for remote-agent pods to ensure eval probes can preempt lower-priority workloads when needed.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-07 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no preemption victims available and preemption not helpful on the affinity-mismatched nodes, every new remote-agent pod was left Unschedulable. The eval runner timed out waiting for the pod to schedule (141 s for remote-agent-state, 122 s for remote-agent-create, 145 s for remote-agent-runtime), exited without producing any evidence, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was therefore entirely unmet. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes advertising the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM never started.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 122s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 141s, latencyMs=145922 — confirms the scheduling failure is not a transient single-pod event.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 145s, latencyMs=151951 — all three remote-agent checks share the same scheduler rejection pattern.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence fields were written, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-ready state.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 (createAgent call) never returned successfully.

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-259): contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because no evidence was produced.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130672 — the probe ran for ~130 s before failing, consistent with a scheduling timeout rather than an immediate API error.
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the two kata/peerpods nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods; if those 2 nodes are also at capacity, no fallback exists. A misconfigured or overly narrow selector would shrink the eligible pool further.

Cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is set too low relative to concurrent demand: multiple simultaneous eval runs or production workloads may be competing for the same finite VM slots.
Peerpods node pool is under-provisioned or a node in the pool is NotReady/cordoned: if one of the two kata-capable nodes is unavailable, effective capacity is halved, making exhaustion more likely.

Preemption policy on the remote-agent pod or the occupying pods prevents eviction: the scheduler explicitly reported 'No preemption victims found', meaning existing pods on those nodes are protected from preemption (e.g., PriorityClass or PodDisruptionBudget).
